title: A Room-by-Room Move-Out Cleaning Checklist
metaDescription: Use this room-by-room move-out cleaning checklist for the kitchen, bathrooms, floors, closets, and final photos. Check your lease before you start.
summary: Move-out cleaning is easier when the home is empty and the work runs from top to bottom, with lease-specific requirements checked first.
transcript: Start with the lease and any move-out instructions from the landlord or property manager. They decide what the property expects, whether carpet cleaning needs a receipt, and how keys are returned. Cleaning can address dirt and residue, but it can't guarantee a deposit because damage, unpaid charges, and lease terms are separate issues.

Work in an empty home. Remove boxes, trash, hangers, food, and anything left in cabinets, closets, the patio, or the garage. If possible, keep the water and electricity on until the cleaning and final inspection are finished.

Then work top to bottom and from dry tasks to wet ones. Dust ceiling fans, light fixtures, vent covers, ledges, and door tops before cleaning counters or floors. Save vacuuming and mopping for the end so you don't do them twice.

In the kitchen, follow the appliance care instructions and clean the oven interior, racks, door glass, cooktop, drip pans, and control area. Wipe inside every empty cabinet and drawer. Degrease the range hood and clean or replace its filter as the manufacturer directs.

Empty and clean the refrigerator and freezer, including shelves, drawers, gaskets, and the floor directly in front of and beside the appliance. Don't pull out a refrigerator that is connected, loaded, or likely to damage the floor. Ask the property manager what they expect and move it only when it can be done safely.

In each bathroom, clean behind and around the toilet, including the bolt caps and the line where the base meets the floor. Wipe the exhaust fan cover, mirror edges, cabinet interiors, fixtures, shower walls, tub, glass, tracks, and accessible grout. Mineral scale may need extra dwell time, but use a product that is safe for the exact surface.

Throughout the rest of the home, clean baseboards, window tracks and sills, door tops, switch plates, handles, closet shelves, rods, and empty built-ins. Remove dust and insects from light covers only if they can be taken down and reinstalled safely with the power off.

Spot-clean walls carefully. Flat paint can turn shiny when scrubbed, and some marks won't come off without taking paint with them. Test a hidden area, use very little moisture, and stop if the finish changes.

Finish with the floors. Vacuum hard floors before mopping so loose grit doesn't become mud. Vacuum carpet slowly in more than one direction, but don't promise that ordinary vacuuming will remove stains or odors. If the lease requires professional carpet cleaning, schedule it separately and keep the receipt.

Before leaving, check the dryer lint screen, under sinks, closet corners, cabinet tops, and the floor around accessible appliances. Don't open electrical panels, disconnect gas appliances, or clean inside mechanical equipment.

Photograph each empty room in good light after the work is finished. Include appliances, cabinet interiors, bathrooms, and floors, then save the move-out inspection and key-return confirmation with those photos. The record won't decide every dispute, but it documents the condition you left behind.
localNote: End-of-month dates and the weeks around NMSU move-in can fill quickly. If your lease ends in late summer, check the requirements and schedule any professional cleaning before the home is packed, not after the truck leaves.

faq.q: Do I have to shampoo the carpet?
faq.a: Check the lease and move-out instructions. Some properties require professional carpet cleaning and a receipt, while others treat it as part of normal turnover. Follow the written requirement instead of guessing.

faq.q: How long does a move-out clean take?
faq.a: It depends on the size, condition, appliances, and mineral buildup. An empty two-bedroom can still take several hours or most of a day, so don't schedule the final walkthrough immediately after you expect to finish.

faq.q: Does professional cleaning guarantee my deposit?
faq.a: No. Cleaning can resolve ordinary dirt and residue, but the landlord controls the inspection and may consider damage, unpaid charges, or other lease terms. A clear scope and final photos give you a better record of the cleaning itself.

faq.q: What if I've already left town?
faq.a: You usually don't need to be present if access, utilities, lockup, and payment are arranged in advance. Make sure the cleaner knows the inspection deadline and exactly how the property should be secured afterward.
